text: # Appointments FAQ ## How long is an appointment? Every appointment is a 30 minute slot. ## What do I need to book an appointment? You need a valid patient ID, a specialty and a date. Pick an open time slot with a doctor and confirm your booking. ## How do I reschedule an appointment? Open My Appointments, click Edit, choose a new date and time, and click Request change. An administrator must approve the request before the appointment moves.

Only one change request can be pending per appointment. ## What happens after I request a change? The appointment keeps its original time and shows Change requested until an administrator approves or rejects it. If someone else books the new time first, the change is rejected and you keep your original time. ## How do I cancel an appointment? Open My Appointments and click Delete on the appointment. The time slot becomes available to other patients straight away. ## Do

I need a referral to book a specialist? No. The booking system does not check for referrals. You can book any specialty directly. ## Can I book an appointment through the chat assistant? No. The assistant can look up appointments and availability, but booking, cancelling and changing appointments must be done on the Book Appointment and My Appointments pages.

# Booking Policy ## Appointment slot length All appointments are booked in fixed 30-minute slots. A doctor's available hours are divided into consecutive 30-minute blocks, and each block can only be booked by one patient at a time. ## Patient ID requirement Every booking requires a valid patient ID. Before an appointment can be created, the system checks that the patient ID exists in the shared patient records. If the ID isn't recognised, the booking is rejected and the patient

is asked to double-check the ID they entered. ## How booking works 1. The patient selects a specialty (e.g. Cardiology, Dermatology) and a date. 2. The system shows every doctor in that specialty who works on that day, along with their open 30-minute slots for that date. 3. Already-booked slots are automatically hidden — a doctor's booked appointments are excluded from what's shown as available. 4. The patient picks an open slot and enters their patient ID to confirm. 5.

If someone else books that exact slot in the moment between viewing and confirming, the booking is rejected and the patient is asked to pick another time. ## Doctor availability Each doctor has a fixed weekly availability window (e.g. "Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00"). Appointments can only be booked within a doctor's stated availability window, on the days they work.

# Cancellation / No-Show Policy # Cancellation Policy ## Cancelling an appointment A patient can cancel an appointment from the My Appointments page by clicking Delete. The appointment is removed from the system. ## What happens to the freed slot Once an appointment is cancelled, its time slot becomes available again straight away and other patients can book it. ## No-shows and late cancellations The system does not track no-shows and has no minimum notice period for cancelling. There is
no penalty for a late cancellation.

# Clinic Hours & Closures ## Current system behavior There is no separate concept of "clinic-wide" opening hours in this system. Availability is set individually per doctor — each doctor has their own weekly availability window (for example, "Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00" or "Tue,Thu 10:00-16:00"). Appointments can only be booked within a doctor's own stated hours, on the days they work. To find out when the clinic is effectively "open," check the combined availability windows of the doctors in a given specialty,

rather than looking for a single clinic-wide schedule. ## Public holidays and closures The system does not currently account for public holidays or one-off closures. If a doctor is normally available on a given day but is actually unavailable due to a holiday or unplanned closure, this isn't reflected in the booking system — a patient could still see and book a slot that won't actually happen. ## Note for the team If clinic-wide hours or holiday closures should exist,
that's a feature that would need to be built (e.g. a closures table checked during availability lookups), not just documented. This file reflects current behavior only.

# Referral Requirements ## Current system behavior This booking system does not currently check or enforce GP referrals for any specialty. A patient can book directly with any specialty — including specialists such as Cardiology, Neurology, or Orthopedics — without needing a referral on file. ## Note for the team Whether referrals should be required for certain specialties is a policy decision that hasn't been made yet for this system. If a referral requirement is added in future, it would

need to be built into the booking flow itself (e.g. checking for a referral record before allowing a booking with a specialist), not just documented here. Until that decision is made, this file reflects the system as it actually works: no referral is required to book any appointment.

# Rescheduling Procedure ## Requesting a change A patient can request to move an existing appointment to a new date and time by submitting a change request. The request includes the appointment being changed and the newly requested date and time. Only one change request can be pending per appointment at a time — if a patient already has a pending request for that appointment, a new one cannot be submitted until the existing one is reviewed. ## What happens

after a request is submitted The appointment itself is not changed immediately. Instead, the request sits in a pending state, visible on the appointment as "Change requested" with the new date and time shown, until an administrator reviews it. ## Admin review An administrator reviews pending change requests and either approves or rejects each one. - **If approved:** the system checks whether the newly requested slot is still free. If it is, the appointment is updated to the new date

and time. If someone else has since booked that slot, the change is rejected instead and the patient keeps their original appointment time. - **If rejected:** the appointment stays at its original date and time, and the patient is notified the request was not approved. Each change request can only be reviewed once — once it's been approved or rejected, it can't be reviewed again.

# Specialty Directory _(Placeholder content — confirm exact specialties and descriptions against your actual doctors table and any clinical guidance from your team before finalising.)_ ## Cardiology Deals with conditions of the heart and blood vessels, including chest pain, high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, and heart disease monitoring. ## Dermatology Deals with skin, hair, and nail conditions, including rashes, acne, moles, and skin infections. ## Pediatrics Deals with the health of infants, children, and adolescents, including routine check-ups, vaccinations, and

childhood illnesses. ## Psychiatry Deals with mental health conditions, including anxiety, depression, and mood disorders, through assessment, therapy referrals, and medication management. ## General Practice The first point of contact for most non-emergency health concerns. General practitioners handle common illnesses, ongoing health management, and referrals to specialists when needed. ## Geriatrics Deals with the health needs of older adults, including managing multiple chronic conditions, mobility, and age-related health concerns. ## Orthopedics Deals with the musculoskeletal system — bones, joints, ligaments,
and muscles — including injuries, fractures, and joint pain. ## Neurology Deals with conditions of the brain, spinal cord, and nervous system, including headaches, seizures, and nerve-related issues.
